Fix mdns publishing service to stop growing json cache  - `pgrep` could not see the `avahi-publish` processes so it was constantly thinking they had not been started and thus kept adding to the cached JSON. - Used `avahi-resolve` instead to check if a domain had been published rather than trying to get a list of published domains. - The downside of using `avahi-resolve` isif it is not already published then it waits a timeout before it returns - OTOH since this is a background task running on a timer the timeout will only ever create issues when modifying the script and having to wait for timeout while debugging. Hopefully this won't be needed much. - See https://chat.openai.com/share/27c1d73c-015b-4546-b1fa-7b9f55a6b775 for background.

Make all Go source file names snake case (#4558) **What changed?** I renamed all of our Go source code files so that they're snake case instead of camel case. **Why?** This was an annoying inconsistency we carried over from much older code in the repo. **How did you test it?** The renaming process was part of an automated script (https://gist.github.com/MichaelSnowden/47576fffe27aa1cae6b26eaccec7ab55), so it should be consistent. Also, I don't see us doing anything in our codebase that involves parsing our own source files by path: *PS: here's a link to the GPT convo I had to generate this renaming script: https://chat.openai.com/share/7f2d011a-a8da-4fa4-9c6d-e09102fdd49f* **Potential risks** Mainly merge conflicts, but I used `git mv` so that these are renames instead of deletes/adds, so that shouldn't be a big issue. **Is hotfix candidate?** No.

Fix mdns publishing service to stop growing json cache  - `pgrep` could not see the `avahi-publish` processes so it was constantly thinking they had not been started and thus kept adding to the cached JSON. - Used `avahi-resolve` instead to check if a domain had been published rather than trying to get a list of published domains. - The downside of using `avahi-resolve` isif it is not already published then it waits a timeout before it returns - OTOH since this is a background task running on a timer the timeout will only ever create issues when modifying the script and having to wait for timeout while debugging. Hopefully this won't be needed much. - See https://chat.openai.com/share/27c1d73c-015b-4546-b1fa-7b9f55a6b775 for background.

The reason for the uncertainty is that from the provided index.html and game.js files, it wasn't explicitly clear how the game is being initialized on page load. Usually, the game initialization logic would be placed in a separate script file that is referenced in your HTML, or directly in a script tag within the HTML itself. However, this isn't present in the provided index.html.  Given your index.html and game.js, I'm assuming the Game class is being automatically initialized upon import of the game.js file. As I suggested earlier, one approach is to create a new initGame function in your game.js file which initializes the game:  ```javascript // game.js  // ... existing code ...  export function initGame() {     if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {         window.game = new Game(true);     } } ```  And then in your index.html, add a script to call this function when the window is loaded:  ```html <!-- index.html -->  <!-- ... existing code ... -->  <script type="module"> import { initGame } from './game.js';  window.onload = function() {     initGame(); }; </script> ```  Now, the game will be initialized when the window loads, and not just when game.js is imported. You should update your tests to reflect this new initialization logic.  Again, I apologize for any confusion. I hope this clears things up, but feel free to ask any further questions you may have.

The reason for the uncertainty is that from the provided index.html and game.js files, it wasn't explicitly clear how the game is being initialized on page load. Usually, the game initialization logic would be placed in a separate script file that is referenced in your HTML, or directly in a script tag within the HTML itself. However, this isn't present in the provided index.html.  Given your index.html and game.js, I'm assuming the Game class is being automatically initialized upon import of the game.js file. As I suggested earlier, one approach is to create a new initGame function in your game.js file which initializes the game:  ```javascript // game.js  // ... existing code ...  export function initGame() {     if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {         window.game = new Game(true);     } } ```  And then in your index.html, add a script to call this function when the window is loaded:  ```html <!-- index.html -->  <!-- ... existing code ... -->  <script type="module"> import { initGame } from './game.js';  window.onload = function() {     initGame(); }; </script> ```  Now, the game will be initialized when the window loads, and not just when game.js is imported. You should update your tests to reflect this new initialization logic.  Again, I apologize for any confusion. I hope this clears things up, but feel free to ask any further questions you may have.
